note: Canonical snack model for the Operation Health Meal Library. Same discipline as #meal-data — the app's Meal Library can import these. Macros are per the stated portion.

tiers.label: Grab & assemble
tiers.blurb: No prep beyond opening a container. Thirty seconds, a bowl, done.

tiers.label: Measure & bag
tiers.blurb: Shelf-stable things that only go wrong when eaten from the bag. Portion once, on a scale, into bags.

tiers.label: Batch & freeze
tiers.blurb: Made in a batch on prep day, same as the meals. Several reuse your 2-Tbsp sauce molds.

snacks.name: Greek yogurt + berries
snacks.portion: ¾ cup nonfat Greek yogurt + ½ cup berries
snacks.note: The best snack in the library: 18g protein for zero fat and almost no sodium. Nothing else here wins on all three.

snacks.name: Protein shake
snacks.portion: 1 scoop + 1 cup skim milk (or water at a desk)
snacks.note: Dry-scoop into a shaker in the morning and add water at your desk — the cheapest 30g of protein you can carry.
snacks.tip: Post-workout this is the one to reach for: liquid protein hits fastest and you're usually not hungry for solid food yet.

snacks.name: ½ protein puck
snacks.portion: Half a 1-cup protein puck, reheated (~2½ oz cooked)
snacks.note: Costs nothing extra — it's already in your freezer from meal prep. Best protein-per-calorie of anything you don't have to shop for.
snacks.tip: Reheat 60–90 seconds from frozen. A squeeze of lime or a spoon of salsa is all it needs.

snacks.name: Cottage cheese + fruit
snacks.portion: ¾ cup 2% cottage cheese + ½ cup pineapple or berries
snacks.note: Macro twin of Greek yogurt but roughly 8× the sodium — a rotation item, not a twice-a-day one.
snacks.tip: Buy 2% (creamy enough to enjoy, only 3g fat) and check the label — mainstream brands run ~600mg sodium where Good Culture is closer to 300mg. If the curds are the problem, see the blended versions below.

snacks.name: Edamame, steamed
snacks.note: 18g protein and 8g fiber for essentially no sodium. Three minutes in the microwave from a frozen bag.
snacks.tip: Salt it at the table, not in the pot — you'll use a fraction as much.

snacks.name: Hard-boiled eggs ×2
snacks.note: Keep a boiled half-dozen in the fridge. Deliberately not tagged for the desk — the smell is an office-etiquette problem.
snacks.tip: Steam them 12 minutes instead of boiling; they peel far more cleanly.

snacks.name: String cheese ×2
snacks.note: Convenient and genuinely portable, but 12g of fat for 14g of protein is a mediocre trade on a day where fat is the ceiling.

snacks.name: Apple + peanut butter
snacks.portion: 1 medium apple + 1 level Tbsp peanut butter
snacks.note: Level the tablespoon. A heaped one is closer to 2 Tbsp and quietly doubles the fat.
snacks.tip: Swap in powdered peanut butter mixed with water and the same snack lands at ~120 kcal and 2g fat.

snacks.name: Deli roll-up — lean
snacks.portion: 4 slices turkey + 2 Tbsp hummus + cucumber batons
snacks.note: The cheese is the entire fat lever in a roll-up — skipping it takes this family from 10g of fat to 3g.
snacks.tip: Buy lower-sodium deli meat. Sodium, not macros, is the real cost of this whole category.

snacks.name: Deli roll-up — classic
snacks.portion: 4 slices turkey + 1 Laughing Cow wedge + cucumber spear
snacks.note: The cucumber spear stands in for a pickle — same shape and crunch, none of the sour.
snacks.tip: Other swaps for the pickle: bell pepper strips (sweet crunch), pepperoncini (tangy, mild heat), or a blanched asparagus spear.

snacks.name: Deli roll-up — Italian
snacks.portion: 3 slices ham + 1 slice provolone + pepperoncini + spinach
snacks.note: The richest and saltiest roll-up. Worth it occasionally; not a default.

snacks.name: Tuna salad — classic
snacks.portion: 1 can chunk light in water, drained + 2 Tbsp nonfat Greek yogurt + lemon + dill + celery + red onion
snacks.note: 27g protein for 1.5g fat — the leanest protein in the library. Greek yogurt instead of mayo saves ~10g of fat and the tang helps with the fish.
snacks.tip: Drain AND rinse the tuna. The packing liquid holds most of the smell, and rinsing is the single biggest improvement you can make.

snacks.name: Tuna salad — creamy horseradish
snacks.portion: 1 can tuna + ¼ cup blended cottage cheese + ½ tsp prepared horseradish + lemon
snacks.note: Horseradish replaces dijon — same sharpness, no mustard. Highest protein-per-calorie of anything on this tab.

snacks.name: Tuna salad — southwest
snacks.portion: 1 can tuna + Greek yogurt + lime + cumin + corn + black beans + cilantro
snacks.note: Deliberately borrows the Southwest Bowl's flavor profile — familiar territory while you get used to fish.

snacks.name: Tuna salad — Mediterranean
snacks.portion: 1 can tuna + lemon + 1 tsp olive oil + capers + cherry tomato + parsley
snacks.note: Capers bring briny sharpness in place of mustard. Serve with cucumber rounds or bell pepper scoops instead of crackers.

snacks.name: Biltong
snacks.note: Air-dried rather than dehydrated, so it's tender rather than leathery — and it carries no added sugar. If jerky has disappointed you before, this fails differently.
snacks.tip: Look for Stryve. 16g protein for 1g fat is the best ratio of any shelf-stable snack here.

snacks.name: Sliced beef jerky
snacks.note: Excellent macros, but one ounce can be your entire day's snack sodium budget. Sliced jerky only — meat sticks like Slim Jims are ~40% fat and a completely different product.
snacks.tip: Jack Link's Original: 10g protein, 6g sugar, 520mg sodium. People's Choice Classic: 9g protein, 9g sugar, but only 270mg sodium. Buy Original, never teriyaki. Note that People's Choice describe their own as "thin and tough" — if texture is your objection, start elsewhere.

snacks.name: Dry-roasted edamame
snacks.note: The most underrated desk snack: shelf-stable, no mess, no smell, 14g protein and 9g fiber. No fridge required.

snacks.name: Roasted chickpeas
snacks.note: Crunchy, cheap, 5g of fiber. Modest protein, so it pairs rather than stands alone.

snacks.name: Air-popped popcorn
snacks.note: An enormous volume of food for nothing — zero added fat, zero sodium, 6g fiber. Popped from bare kernels, not from a bag.
snacks.tip: Kernels in a brown paper lunch bag, fold the top twice, microwave ~2 min until pops slow to 2 seconds apart. Season after: spray oil plus nutritional yeast (cheesy, adds a little protein), chili-lime, or everything bagel. Two pounds of kernels runs about $3 and makes ~26 bags' worth. Pair it with a blended cottage cheese dip to fix its near-zero protein.

snacks.name: Almonds, portioned
snacks.note: 14g of fat is nearly a fifth of your daily budget for 6g of protein. This single line is why the measure-and-bag tier exists — never eat these from the container.
snacks.tip: Buy unsalted. Salted runs ~190mg sodium for no benefit.

snacks.name: Trail mix, weighed
snacks.note: Low protein, high fat, easy to overeat. Fine as an occasional desk item; not a default.

snacks.name: Egg bites ×2
snacks.note: Freeze a tray; reheat 60–90 seconds. Portable once cooled.

snacks.name: Turkey meatballs ×3
snacks.note: Make a double batch on Italian Bowl prep day and freeze the overflow as a snack. Zero extra shopping.

snacks.name: Smoothie freezer pack
snacks.note: Bag frozen fruit, spinach and oats in portions on prep day. Tip a bag into the blender, add protein powder and water.
snacks.tip: The biggest snack on the tab — treat it as a post-workout meal rather than a top-up.

snacks.name: Greek yogurt bark
snacks.note: Reuses your sixteen 2-Tbsp sauce molds — zero new equipment. Frozen yogurt that happens to be 12g of protein.

snacks.name: Blended cottage cheese — everything bagel dip
snacks.portion: ¾ cup blended + everything seasoning + squeeze of lemon
snacks.note: Thirty seconds in the blender turns curds into something like whipped ricotta. If texture was the objection, this is the fix.
snacks.tip: This is the dip that pairs with air-popped popcorn — together ~275 kcal, 20g protein, and a genuinely large pile of food.

snacks.name: Blended cottage cheese — ranch dip
snacks.portion: ¾ cup blended + dried dill, garlic & onion powder, chives
snacks.note: Dip for cucumber, peppers, carrots. Makes vegetables into a 15g-protein snack.

snacks.name: Blended cottage cheese — chocolate pudding
snacks.portion: ¾ cup blended + 1 Tbsp cocoa + sweetener
snacks.note: Dessert that is 16g of protein and 3g of fat. This is the whole evening strategy in one bowl.

snacks.name: Blended cottage cheese — honey-vanilla whip
snacks.portion: ¾ cup blended + 1 tsp honey + vanilla + cinnamon, over berries
snacks.note: Tastes like cheesecake filling. Also good dolloped on hot food with Italian herbs instead of honey — a passable ricotta.

snacks.name: Protein hot chocolate
snacks.portion: 1 scoop chocolate protein + 1 tsp cocoa + hot skim milk or water
snacks.note: The sleeper for an evening craving — warm and slow to drink, which does more than anything cold. 26g of protein disguised as dessert.
snacks.tip: Mix the powder into a splash of cold liquid first, then top up with hot. Straight into hot liquid and it clumps.

snacks.name: Frozen grapes
snacks.note: The sweet equivalent of air-popped popcorn — eat a whole bowl and pay nothing. Freezing makes them slow to eat, which is most of the point.
snacks.tip: No protein at all, so pair with the chocolate pudding or hot chocolate if it's replacing a real snack.

snacks.name: No-bake protein oat bar
snacks.note: Store bars run $2.50–3.50 and 15–20g of fat. These are ~$0.75 and 4g, because powdered peanut butter binds as well as the real thing.

snacks.name: Baked protein oat bar
snacks.note: Cakier than the no-bake version and the lowest-fat bar of the three. Wraps in parchment, survives a bag.

snacks.name: Protein crispy treat
snacks.note: A rice-crispy treat that is 12g of protein and 2g of fat. Aimed squarely at the evening sweet tooth.

makeYourOwn.name: Homemade Greek yogurt
makeYourOwn.time: 20 min hands-on · 8–12 hr culture · 2–4 hr strain
makeYourOwn.why: About $0.50 a cup against ~$1.25 store-bought. On something you eat every single day, that adds up faster than anything else in the library.
makeYourOwn.warn: Use SKIM milk. Whole-milk yogurt runs ~10g fat per ¾ cup — on a daily item that's an eighth of your fat budget appearing out of nowhere. Skim reproduces your current tub almost exactly.
ingredients: 1 gallon skim milk
2 Tbsp of your current store yogurt (the starter — it just needs live cultures)
steps: Heat the milk to 180°F — Instant Pot on Boil, or a heavy pot on the stove. This denatures the whey proteins and is what makes the yogurt thick. Do not skip it.
Cool to 110°F. A sink of cold water speeds this up.
Whisk in the 2 Tbsp of starter yogurt until fully dispersed.
Hold at 108–112°F for 8–12 hours — Instant Pot Yogurt setting, or an oven with just the light on. Longer means tangier.
Strain 2–4 hours through cheesecloth or a nut-milk bag over a bowl. This is the step that makes it Greek.
Save 2 Tbsp of this batch as the starter for the next one.
tips: The strained-off whey is protein-rich — use it in smoothies instead of pouring it away.
Keeps about 2 weeks in the fridge.

makeYourOwn.name: Homemade jerky
makeYourOwn.time: 20 min prep · 6–24 hr marinade · 3–4 hr dry
makeYourOwn.why: Store-bought runs ~$2.00/oz. Eye of round at ~$7/lb works out to ~$1.30/oz — roughly half. More importantly you control the two things you can't buy your way out of: drop the sugar entirely and halve the sodium.
ingredients: 2–3 lbs eye of round (leanest and cheapest; top round also works)
½ cup soy sauce (low-sodium)
2 Tbsp Worcestershire
1 tsp each garlic powder, onion powder, coarse black pepper
1 tsp liquid smoke
steps: Trim every visible speck of fat. Fat goes rancid — it's the reason jerky must be made from lean cuts.
Freeze the meat 1–2 hours so it firms up and slices cleanly.
Slice ¼ inch thick, AGAINST the grain. This is your tenderness lever — with the grain is what makes jerky leathery.
Marinate 6–24 hours in the fridge. No sugar needed.
Pat dry, then dry at 160–180°F in the air fryer for 2–3 hours, or at 175°F in the oven with the door cracked for 3–4 hours.
Done when a piece cracks but does not snap. Pull earlier than feels right — over-drying is the usual reason people think they dislike jerky.
tips: Food safety: either bring the meat to 160°F internal before drying, or finish the dried jerky at 275°F for 10 minutes.
Store in the fridge ~2 weeks, or freeze for months.

makeYourOwn.name: Homemade protein bars
makeYourOwn.time: 15 min · plus chill or 20 min bake
makeYourOwn.why: Store bars cost $2.50–3.50 each and usually carry 15–20g of fat. These run $0.60–0.90 and 2–4g. The trick is that most recipes lean on nut butter to bind — swapping in powdered peanut butter, Greek yogurt or pumpkin purée binds just as well at a fraction of the fat. You already buy protein powder for shakes, so the marginal cost is oats and a binder.
ingredients: No-bake: 2 cups oats · 2 scoops protein powder · ½ cup powdered peanut butter (PB2) mixed with water · ⅓ cup honey · milk to bind
Baked: 2 cups oats · 2 scoops protein powder · 4 egg whites · ¾ cup applesauce · cinnamon · 1 tsp baking powder
Crispy: 2 scoops protein powder · 3 cups brown rice cereal · ½ cup marshmallow or honey · splash of milk
steps: No-bake — mix everything, press hard into a parchment-lined 8×8 pan, chill 2 hours, cut into 8. Press harder than you think or they crumble.
Baked — mix, spread in an 8×8 pan, bake at 350°F for 18–22 minutes until just set. Cool fully before cutting.
Crispy — melt the marshmallow or honey, stir in the protein powder off the heat, fold through the cereal, press into the pan and cool.
Wrap individually in parchment. They keep a week in the fridge and freeze for months.
tips: Whey protein bakes drier than casein or a blend. If your bars come out chalky, add another ¼ cup of applesauce or milk.
Pull the baked bars while they still look slightly underdone — they firm up as they cool.

makeYourOwn.name: Blended cottage cheese base
makeYourOwn.why: Cottage cheese's only real problem is the curds. Thirty seconds in a blender turns it into something like whipped ricotta, and it stops being cottage cheese at all — it becomes a base that goes five directions.
ingredients: 1½ cups 2% cottage cheese (low-sodium if you can find it)
steps: Blend on high 30 seconds, scraping down once, until completely smooth with no grain left.

Split into portions and flavor each one: everything bagel seasoning + lemon · dried dill, garlic and onion powder, chives · cocoa and sweetener · honey, vanilla and cinnamon · Italian herbs for a ricotta stand-in.
tips: The savory versions are dips — cucumber, peppers, carrots, and air-popped popcorn.
Sodium is the one weak spot: a serving is 450–550mg. Low-sodium cottage cheese cuts that nearly in half.

makeYourOwn.name: Greek yogurt bark
makeYourOwn.why: Reuses the sixteen 2-Tbsp sauce molds you already own, so there's no new equipment and no new shopping. Frozen dessert at 12g protein and 3g fat a serving.
ingredients: 2 cups nonfat Greek yogurt
2 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
1 tsp vanilla
Berries, chopped; a little dark chocolate if you want it
steps: Stir the yogurt with honey and vanilla.
Spoon into the 2-Tbsp molds, pressing a berry or two into each.
Freeze 3 hours until solid, pop out, and bag. Keeps 2 months.
Eat straight from the freezer — 4 pieces is a serving.
tips: Skip the chocolate to keep it at 3g of fat; a tablespoon of chips across the batch adds about 1g per serving.

makeYourOwn.name: Egg bites
makeYourOwn.why: Freezer-friendly, portable once cooled, and they use up whatever veg is left from meal prep.
ingredients: 6 whole eggs + 4 egg whites
¼ cup cottage cheese (blended in — this is what makes them custardy)
Chopped peppers, onion, spinach; a little cheese
Salt, pepper
steps: Blend the eggs, whites and cottage cheese until smooth.
Divide veg between 12 greased muffin cups, pour the egg mix over.
Bake at 325°F for 20–22 minutes until just set — low and slow keeps them tender.
Cool completely, then freeze on a tray before bagging.
tips: Using more whites than yolks is the fat lever: all-whole-egg bites are closer to 14g of fat per pair.

makeYourOwn.name: Roasted chickpeas
makeYourOwn.why: Cheap, crunchy, 5g of fiber a portion, and shelf-stable enough for a desk drawer for a few days.
ingredients: 2 cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
2 tsp olive oil
Smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt
steps: Dry the chickpeas thoroughly on a towel — this is the difference between crunchy and chewy. Rub the skins off as you go.
Toss with oil and spices.
Air fryer 15–18 min at 390°F shaking twice, or oven 40 min at 400°F.
Cool completely uncovered before bagging, or they go soft.
tips: They soften after a couple of days — make a batch you'll finish inside a week.
Season after roasting for a punchier flavor.

makeYourOwn.name: Air-popped popcorn
makeYourOwn.why: Bagged popcorn is 36% fat by weight; microwave bags are close behind. The corn was never the problem — you're paying for the oil it arrives in. A whole SkinnyPop bag is 675 kcal and 45g of fat; the same volume air-popped is about 230 kcal and under 3g.
ingredients: ¼ cup popcorn kernels
Spray oil, nutritional yeast, chili-lime or everything bagel seasoning
steps: Put the kernels in a brown paper lunch bag and fold the top over twice. No oil, no staples.
Microwave on high ~2 minutes, until the pops slow to about 2 seconds apart. Listen, don't trust the timer.
Tip into a bowl, mist lightly with spray oil, then season.
tips: Nutritional yeast gives it a cheesy hit and adds a little protein.
Two pounds of kernels costs about $3 and makes roughly 26 bags' worth.
Popcorn has almost no protein — pair it with a blended cottage cheese dip to make it a real snack.

makeYourOwn.name: Canned tuna — a primer
makeYourOwn.why: One can drained is 100 kcal, 22g protein and 1g fat — the leanest protein available to you. Worth pushing through the taste barrier, because nothing else in the library is this efficient.
makeYourOwn.warn: Keep this one at home. The macros are excellent but tuna at a desk is an office-etiquette problem.
ingredients: Solid white albacore in water (milder than chunk light while you adjust)
steps: Drain AND rinse. The packing liquid holds most of the smell — this is the single biggest improvement available.
Hit it with acid immediately: lemon juice, or a splash of vinegar. This isn't just flavor-masking — acid binds the trimethylamine that is the fishy smell and stops it going airborne.
Mix with nonfat Greek yogurt rather than mayo. Saves ~10g of fat and the tang helps again.
Don't make it the star at first — fold it into a bowl or onto a tortilla with something loud.
tips: Not a mustard fan? Prepared horseradish (½ tsp) is the sharpest swap and a completely different flavor family. Minced capers or a splash of vinegar also work.
Serve with cucumber rounds or bell pepper scoops instead of crackers.
